app.name: Google Photos: Backup & Edit
app.description: Google Photos backs up your photos and videos to the cloud, uses AI to organize and search them, and offers editing tools. Part of Google services.

verdict.one_liner: Google analyzes your uploaded photos and videos, but does not use them for personalized ads.
verdict.summary: Google Photos automatically backs up photos and videos you upload to Google's cloud. The Google Privacy Policy states that Google uses automated systems to analyze your content to provide features tailored to how you use its services, and that uploaded photos and videos are used to help create albums and other creations. Importantly, the policy explicitly states that Google does not show personalized ads based on your content from Photos. However, your general activity across Google services may still be used for ads depending on your settings, and everything is linked to your Google Account.
verdict.recommendation_reason: Google Photos is convenient for backup, but Google analyzes your uploaded content with automated systems and links your activity to your Google Account. If privacy matters, consider Apple Photos with iCloud instead.

red.title: Google uses automated systems to analyze your uploads
red.plain_english: Google's privacy policy states that it uses automated systems that analyze your content to provide features tailored to how you use its services. It also says photos and videos you upload to Google Photos are used to help you create albums and other creations.

red.title: Your Photos activity is linked to your Google Account
red.plain_english: Google's privacy policy states that when you are signed in, information is collected and stored with your Google Account and treated as personal information.

red.title: Location information is collected when you use Google services
red.plain_english: Google's privacy policy states that it collects location information when you use its services, including for ads and search results. It does not clearly explain whether Google Photos specifically extracts location from your photo metadata.

red.title: Your activity across Google services may be used for ads
red.plain_english: Google's privacy policy states that depending on your settings, it may show you personalized ads based on your interests and activity across Google services. However, the policy explicitly states that Google does not show personalized ads based on your content from Photos.

green.title: Encryption protects data in transit
green.plain_english: Google's privacy policy states that it uses encryption to keep your data private while in transit.

green.title: You can delete your Photos content and account
green.plain_english: Google's privacy policy states that you can delete your content from specific Google services, delete specific Google products, or delete your entire Google Account. You can also export a copy of your content.

green.title: Google does not use your Photos content for personalized ads
green.plain_english: Google's privacy policy explicitly states that it does not show you personalized ads based on your content from Photos.

categories.label: Camera & Microphone
categories.plain_english: Camera access is used when you take photos directly within the app. Microphone access is optional and used for video recording.
categories.detail: Google Photos can access your camera to take new photos and videos. This is optional since you can also upload existing photos from your library.

categories.label: Location & GPS
categories.plain_english: Google collects location information when you use its services. The policy does not clearly explain whether Google Photos specifically reads location data embedded in your uploads.
categories.detail: The general Google Privacy Policy says location is collected for driving directions, search results, and ads. It does not specifically mention extracting EXIF location metadata from uploaded photos.
categories.policy_excerpt: We collect location information when you use our services, which helps us offer features like driving directions, search results for things near you, and ads based on your location.
concerns: Policy does not clearly explain whether photo location metadata is extracted

categories.label: Contacts & Phonebook
categories.plain_english: The policy does not mention whether Google Photos accesses your phone contacts.
categories.detail: The general Google Privacy Policy mentions suggesting recipients from your contacts when sharing content, but does not explicitly state whether Photos accesses contacts.
concerns: Policy silent on contact access for Photos

categories.label: Storage & File Access
categories.plain_english: Google Photos needs access to your photo library to back up and store your photos and videos on Google's cloud servers.
categories.detail: Full photo library access is required for the app's core backup function. The policy states that photos and videos you upload are used to help create albums and other creations.
categories.policy_excerpt: We also collect the content you create, upload, or receive from others when using our services. This includes things like email you write and receive, photos and videos you save, docs and spreadsheets you create.
concerns: All uploaded photos are stored on Google's servers
Automated systems analyze your uploaded content

categories.label: Data Sharing with 3rd Parties
categories.plain_english: Google's privacy policy states that personal information is shared with affiliates and trusted businesses for external processing, and non-personally identifiable information is shared with partners including advertisers.
categories.detail: The policy says Google does not share personal information outside of Google except with consent, domain administrators, for external processing, or for legal reasons. However, it also says non-personally identifiable information may be shared publicly and with partners like publishers, advertisers, and developers.
categories.policy_excerpt: We do not share your personal information with companies, organizations, or individuals outside of Google except in the following cases: With your consent; With domain administrators; For external processing; For legal reasons. We may share non-personally identifiable information publicly and with our partners — like publishers, advertisers, developers, or rights holders.
concerns: Data shared with Google's external processors
Non-personally identifiable information shared with advertisers

categories.label: Account & Identity Data
categories.plain_english: You need a Google Account to use Google Photos. Google collects your name, email, and phone number, and links your Photos activity to your broader Google identity.
categories.detail: A Google Account is required. The policy states that when you create an account, you provide personal information including your name and password, and you can add a phone number or payment information. When signed in, information is stored with your Google Account.
categories.policy_excerpt: When you create a Google Account, you provide us with personal information that includes your name and a password. You can also choose to add a phone number or payment information to your account. When you're signed in, we also collect information that we store with your Google Account, which we treat as personal information.
concerns: Activity combined across all Google services

categories.label: Behavioural & Ad Tracking
categories.plain_english: Google may use your activity across services for personalized ads depending on your settings, but it explicitly says it does not use your Photos content for ads.
categories.detail: The general policy says depending on your settings, Google may show personalized ads based on your activity across services. However, the policy explicitly states: 'We don't show you personalized ads based on your content from Drive, Gmail, or Photos.'
categories.policy_excerpt: Depending on your settings, we may also show you personalized ads based on your interests and activity across Google services. We don't show you personalized ads based on your content from Drive, Gmail, or Photos.
concerns: General activity may be used for ads

categories.label: Children's Data Handling
categories.plain_english: Google offers Family Link for children under 13.
categories.detail: The general Google Privacy Policy references Family Link for children under the applicable age.
categories.policy_excerpt: Google Accounts Managed with Family Link, for Children under 13 (or applicable age in your country)

categories.label: Network & Internet Activity
categories.plain_english: Google logs your IP address, device info, and system activity continuously when you use Google services.
categories.detail: The policy states that Google collects information about the interaction of your apps, browsers, and devices with its services, including IP address, crash reports, and system activity.
categories.policy_excerpt: We collect information about the interaction of your apps, browsers, and devices with our services, including IP address, crash reports, system activity, and the date, time, and referrer URL of your request.

categories.label: Device Info & Fingerprinting
categories.plain_english: Google collects detailed information about your device including unique identifiers, operating system, and carrier.
categories.detail: The policy says Google collects unique identifiers, browser type, device type and settings, operating system, mobile network information including carrier name and phone number, and application version number.
categories.policy_excerpt: The information we collect includes unique identifiers, browser type and settings, device type and settings, operating system, mobile network information including carrier name and phone number, and application version number.
concerns: Carrier name and phone number collected

categories.label: Health & Biometric Data
categories.plain_english: The Google Privacy Policy does not mention collecting health or biometric data for Google Photos.
categories.detail: No health or biometric data collection is referenced in the privacy policy for Google Photos.

categories.label: Financial & Payment Data
categories.plain_english: If you upgrade to Google One for extra storage, Google collects payment information through its payment processors.
categories.detail: The policy mentions that Google processes your payment information when you buy extra storage for Google Drive. This would apply to Google One storage upgrades for Photos as well.
categories.policy_excerpt: We process your payment information when you buy extra storage for Google Drive.

categories.label: Data Deletion & User Rights
categories.plain_english: You can delete individual photos, albums, or your entire Google Account. Google Takeout lets you download your data first. Some data may be retained for legal or security reasons.
categories.detail: The policy provides tools to delete content from specific services or your entire account. Some data is retained for legal, security, and abuse prevention purposes.
categories.policy_excerpt: Delete your content from specific Google services. Delete specific Google products. Delete your entire Google Account. And some data we retain for longer periods of time when necessary for legitimate business or legal purposes.
concerns: Some data retained after deletion for legal/security reasons

categories.label: Policy Change Notification
categories.plain_english: Google promises not to reduce your rights under its Privacy Policy without your explicit consent, and it provides more prominent notice for significant changes.
categories.detail: The general Google Privacy Policy states it will not reduce your rights without explicit consent, and provides more prominent notice for significant changes.
categories.policy_excerpt: We change this Privacy Policy from time to time. We will not reduce your rights under this Privacy Policy without your explicit consent. If changes are significant, we'll provide a more prominent notice.
